note.after_visit_summary: Your mood has been steady lately, and your checkup today went well. Your heart rate and blood pressure are normal, and your liver and kidney tests were all fine. You feel bright and relaxed, and your thinking and speech are normal. You are taking lamotrigine 200 mg once a day, which is still working well. Before we do anything else, you mentioned your gynecologist wants to start you on birth control pills (norgestimate and ethinyl estradiol) next month. These pills can lower the level of lamotrigine in your body, so we need to be careful. This week, you will have a blood test for lamotrigine before you take your morning dose. When you start the birth control pills, we will recheck the level in 2 to 3 weeks, and your lamotrigine dose may need to be raised. Ask your gynecologist about a birth control method that does not use estrogen. Keep taking your multivitamin. If you get a rash, especially with fever or mouth sores, stop lamotrigine and call us or go to the emergency room. If you miss 5 or more days in a row, do not restart at 200 mg on your own; call us. Call us at 317-555-0172 with lab results or any concerns. See you in 3 months, or sooner if things change.
